name: Serbian SuperLiga
content:
The Serbian SuperLiga, established in 2006 following the restructuring of Serbian football, became the highest level of professional football competition in Serbia. Since its foundation, the league has brought together clubs from across the country and has served as the main stage for the nation’s strongest teams to compete for domestic success and qualification to European tournaments.

Between 2006 and 2023, a total of 39 different clubs participated in the competition, reflecting the changing landscape of Serbian football. While many teams have appeared in the league over the years, only a small number consistently challenged for the championship, with the title race largely dominated by Serbia’s traditional football powers.

The rivalry between Red Star and Partizan has defined the SuperLiga era. After 20 seasons, Red Star secured 12 championship titles, while Partizan won 8. Red Star also set a remarkable record by claiming seven consecutive league titles, establishing one of the most dominant periods in the history of Serbian domestic football.

name: Serbian Cup
content:
The Serbian Cup is the national knockout football competition in Serbia, established in 2006 after the dissolution of the state union between Serbia and Montenegro. Organized by the Football Association of Serbia, it serves as the country’s primary cup tournament and gives its winner a place in European competition qualification. The tournament succeeded earlier cup competitions that existed during the Yugoslav and Serbia and Montenegro eras.

The competition introduced a new identity after Serbia became independent, including a newly designed trophy selected through a contest at Belgrade’s Art College. The winning design, inspired by Serbian history and Orthodox traditions, became a symbolic part of the tournament. The first Serbian Cup final took place in 2007, when Red Star defeated Vojvodina and became the inaugural champion of the independent competition.

Since its creation, the Serbian Cup has been dominated by the country’s biggest clubs, especially Red Star and Partizan. Red Star has become the most successful club in the competition, while several other teams such as Vojvodina, Čukarički, and Jagodina have also achieved memorable victories. Over time, the tournament has remained an important part of Serbian football by offering both domestic prestige and a pathway to European football.
